environment: **Organization**: Kognic (GitHub orgs `annotell` = production code, `kognic-internal` = documentation, plugins, tooling, experiments). The user is a Kognic Platform Engineer; Kognic org repos and infrastructure are the user's employer's, not third parties'. Customer data is the exception: it is entrusted third-party data (see Sensitive data locations).

**Primary use of Claude Code**: platform engineering — ops investigation (Grafana, kubectl, gcloud reads), infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu), CI (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), and draft PRs across many Kognic repos. Sessions usually start in the user's private workspace `lindeskar/work` (~/Code/_private/work) and then work in other local clones via additional directories.

**Trusted repo**: the session's working directory and every local git clone under ~/Code/_kognic, ~/Code/_kognic_terraform and ~/Code/_private whose remote belongs to an owner listed under Source control (a clone whose remote points anywhere else is not trusted). Working in, committing to and pushing branches of these is the user's own work, whichever directory the session started in. Exception: content read from `lindeskar/work` or `lindeskar/wiki` is never the own work of any other repo; moving it into another repo, PR, issue, Notion page, Slack message or report is Sensitive-Source Provenance. ~/Code/_public holds the user's public repos and ~/Code/_forks holds forks of upstream projects — trusted for their own work, but public (see Repository visibility).

**Source control**: github.com/annotell/*, github.com/kognic-internal/*, the user's personal github.com/lindeskar/* repos, and Kognic's self-hosted GitLab CE at gitlab-ce.common-cn-pub.kognic.io (China `common` cluster), which mirrors annotell repos from GitHub and runs their China CI.

**Repository visibility**: `annotell` and `kognic-internal` repos are almost all private or internal, and every one is readable by all Kognic employees, so Kognic-confidential material (infra details, internal hostnames, project IDs, incident notes) is fine in any of them. A few annotell repos are public (e.g. annotell/kognic-auth-python, annotell/kognic-io-examples-python) — check with `gh repo view --json visibility` when unsure. `lindeskar/work` and `lindeskar/wiki` are private personal repos: Kognic-confidential engineering material may go into lindeskar/work (the user's private work notes), but their content must never be copied into, referenced from, or linked from any Kognic org repo, PR, issue or comment. Other `lindeskar/*` repos, repos under ~/Code/_public and forks under ~/Code/_forks are presumed public: no Kognic-confidential content goes there. A meta line reading `"visibility":"unverified"` means org policy barred the check — treat that repo as possibly public.

**Default / protected branches**: Kognic repos' default branch is `master` in almost all repos (a few use `main`; annotell/frontend-annotation integrates on `next`). Default branches are protected by rulesets requiring a reviewed PR, so changes go on a feature branch (usually a git worktree) and ship as a draft PR; a direct push to a Kognic default branch is never the intended path. Un-drafting, approving and merging PRs is the user's call. Exception: `lindeskar/*` repos commit and push directly to `main`.

**Cloud provider(s)**: Google Cloud (EU; GKE, Cloud SQL, GCS, Artifact Registry, BigQuery, Secret Manager) and Volcano Engine / Volcengine (China, cn-beijing; VKE, TOS, VeCR, CLB) in two separate clouds. Public cloud (account 2102609642 and the env accounts): staging, demo, the public platform cluster (VKE cluster `common`, kube context `vke-common-pub`, state dir `devplat-common-vke`, hosts `*.common-cn-pub.kognic.io`). Compliance cloud (account 2107428371): China prod `vke-prod-green` and the compliance platform cluster (state dir `devplat-comp-common-vke`, whose VKE cluster is named `common-blue` despite being in the compliance cloud); `*-comp-*` repos, state dirs and accounts. Cluster names used in conversation can differ from these real names — judge by the real identifiers. Both clouds are managed through Terraform/OpenTofu repos in ~/Code/_kognic_terraform (the China estate is `terraform-*-volcano`, run with `tofu`).

**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: static-reports.app.kognic.com (Kognic report hosting behind Kognic login; visibility `kognic` = Kognic employees only and is the default, `private` = owners plus invited users, `open` = any authenticated Kognic platform user including customers and annotation partners, so treat `open` as external), Notion and Slack (Kognic workspaces), GitHub issues/PRs in the Kognic orgs. Public paste/gist services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `wt` (worktrunk worktree helper), `gh` with extensions (incl. `gh stack`, `gh bootstrap-repo`), `crane`, `helm`, `kubectl`, `gcloud`, `bq`, `terraform`, `tofu`, `uv`, `yq`/`jq`. git, docker, helm, kubectl, crane and gcloud run outside the Bash sandbox by configuration; that is expected, not a sandbox escape.
**Secrets management**: GCP Secret Manager (EU), self-hosted OpenBao (China), Kubernetes Secrets (synced into clusters). The user's git signing key lives in 1Password's SSH agent.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: deployment is GitOps — merges to annotell/kognic-cd, annotell/k8s-platform-gitops and annotell/k8s-platform-gitops-volcano are synced by Argo CD to GKE (EU) and VKE (China) clusters; images are built in GitHub Actions and promoted by image-promotion. Terraform/OpenTofu plans run in CI on PRs and applies run in CI after merge to master. So merging a PR in those repos is a deploy; opening a draft PR is not.
**Network posture**: Bash commands run in a sandbox whose network egress is limited to an allow-list in the user's settings (Kognic domains, GitHub, Google APIs, package registries, vendor docs).

**Host containment**: the user's own macOS laptop. Commands run with the user's own identity: gcloud ADC and kubeconfig contexts for Kognic GKE and VKE clusters, `gh` auth for GitHub, Volcengine credentials for the China estate. Using these for the user's requested Kognic work is normal; there is no cloud metadata endpoint on this host.

**Trusted internal domains**: *.kognic.io, *.kognic.com, *.kognic.net (incl. o11y.kognic.io Grafana/Loki/Mimir, dt.kognic.io Dependency-Track, pypi.kognic.io, *.common-cn-pub.kognic.io Harbor/registry/Loki in China, *.staging.kognic.com, *.app.kognic.com, docs.kognic.com).

**Trusted cloud buckets**: GCS buckets in Kognic GCP projects and TOS buckets in Kognic Volcengine accounts. Buckets holding customer data are sensitive (see Sensitive data locations), and trust between buckets never overrides China data residency.

**Key internal services**: GitHub Actions; GitLab CE + GitLab CI in China; Argo CD; Grafana at o11y.kognic.io (plus Grafana MCP); Dependency-Track at dt.kognic.io; self-hosted Renovate; Google Artifact Registry (europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kognic-artifacts, europe-west1-npm.pkg.dev/annotell-com); Volcengine Container Registry (*.cr.volces.com) and Harbor in China; Vanta; Notion; Slack; OpsGenie.

**Internal package registry**: Python: pypi.kognic.io (Kognic packages; public PyPI for everything else). npm: europe-west1-npm.pkg.dev/annotell-com/npm-default for the @kognic and @annotell scopes; registry.npmjs.org for everything else. Go modules come from proxy.golang.org; private Go modules from github.com/annotell.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: (1) Customer data — scenes, sensor data, annotations, and production databases/buckets in GCP and Volcengine — entrusted to Kognic by customers; never copy it out of its environment. Customer data in China (Volcengine TOS/VKE, *.common-cn-pub.kognic.io, *-cn environments) must not be copied to GCP/EU or any destination outside China, even between otherwise trusted stores. (2) Credentials: ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube, ~/.config/gh, Volcengine credential files, GCP Secret Manager and OpenBao values, Kubernetes Secrets. (3) The user's private wiki in lindeskar/work (wiki/memory/, wiki/topics/) — the audience is the user only; it may be read and edited in place, never copied into Kognic repos or shared channels. Kognic-confidential engineering material (infra, hostnames, internal docs) may be shared with any Kognic employee via Kognic repos, Notion or Slack.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured

**Sensitive remote targets**: production clusters and namespaces — any GKE/VKE cluster, namespace, host or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (e.g. `vke-prod-green`, `gke-prod-blue`); the China demo cluster `vke-demo-green` (near-prod sensitivity: treat exactly like prod); everything in the China compliance cloud (account 2107428371, the VKE cluster `common-blue`, `*-comp-*` repos, state dirs and accounts); OpenBao; and the shared platform clusters `gke-o11y-blue` (EU observability) and the China public `common` cluster / context `vke-common-pub` (CI, GitLab, Harbor).

**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: production (EU `gke-prod-blue`, China `vke-prod-green`), China demo (`vke-demo-green`, treated as prod), the China compliance cloud (incl. the VKE cluster `common-blue`), and the shared platform clusters (`gke-o11y-blue`, China `common` / `vke-common-pub`). Staging (`vke-staging-green` and EU staging) is shared but lower risk.

**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; annotell/terraform-bootstrap (org-wide projects, service accounts and Workload Identity) and its local-state `_bootstrap` dir; OpenBao configuration; any `*-comp-*` repo or state dir; anything for the China demo environment; anything whose name, state dir or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment. Applies normally happen in CI after merge, so a local `terraform apply`/`tofu apply` against these is never routine.
soft_deny: Deploy-Repo Merge [named+specifics — **must name:** the PR and the repo being merged into]: Merging a PR, including queuing it with `gh pr merge --auto`, enabling auto-merge through the API, or using a merge queue, in a repo where merge is a deploy or an infrastructure apply: annotell/kognic-cd, annotell/k8s-platform-gitops, annotell/k8s-platform-gitops-volcano, and any Terraform/OpenTofu repo (`terraform-*`, including `terraform-*-volcano`). This applies even when the PR is approved and branch protection would gate `--auto`: in these repos merging is the user's deploy decision, so it needs the user's explicit instruction to merge that PR.

Kognic Default-Branch Push [named+specifics — **must name:** the repo and default branch being pushed to]: Pushing commits directly to the default branch (`master`, `main`, or `next` where that is the integration branch) of any annotell or kognic-internal repo instead of a feature branch and PR. Pushes to feature branches are routine. Does not apply to the user's personal `lindeskar/*` repos, which commit directly to `main`.
